solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Outline of potential reason one’s on a trip still (6)

indicators.note: a word's outline is its two outer letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of 'potential'
acid (LSD) is what sends a user on a trip

annotation.surface: Someone sketches out why a traveller might be on a journey at all.
annotation.walkthrough: The trip is a drug trip, not a journey, and 'still' at the end is the adjective meaning calm, not the adverb.
annotation.definitionFit: Still water and placid water are both calm and undisturbed.

clue.text: Where to see art primarily like work snubbed by European (6)

indicators.note: take only the first letter
the European turns his back on the work, so one E leaves it

blocks.note: an artist's oeuvre is their body of work
the standard abbreviation, removed from OEUVRE to leave OUVRE

annotation.surface: A gallery-goer is told where the art is, like something a European critic sniffed at.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Primarily' sits right after 'art' and seems to take its A, but it applies to 'like', which follows it.
annotation.definitionFit: The Louvre in Paris is the world's most visited art museum.

clue.text: Appeared woke and frivolous (4,2,5)

blocks.note: to come to is to wake up
light as in light-hearted or trivial

annotation.surface: Someone is sneered at as looking both politically woke and shallow.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Woke' reads as the modern political label, but it is simply the past tense of wake.
annotation.definitionFit: Something that came to light appeared or emerged into view.

clue.text: Like a poet’s Hamlet, say, carrying quest off (9)

definitions.note: Read 'Like a poet's' as 'like a (certain) poet's work', an adjective.

indicators.note: DANE carries the other letters inside it
the letters of QUEST go off, out of order

annotation.surface: A remark that a poet's version of Hamlet sets out on a quest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hamlet, say' is the example-of pattern: Hamlet is one instance of a Dane. The poet in question is Dante.
annotation.definitionFit: Dantesque means in the style of Dante, the poet of the Divine Comedy.

clue.text: Name that is ushering in artistic work? (8)

definitions.text: Name that is ushering in artistic work?

indicators.note: IE ushers OP inside itself

blocks.note: to name something is to call it

annotation.surface: A question asking for the name of whoever introduces a work of art.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: Calliope is a Muse, one who ushers in (inspires) artistic work.
annotation.definitionFit: Calliope is the Muse of epic poetry, a named figure who inspires artistic creation.

clue.text: Expert on the fiddle in business, one banking on a couple of pounds (7)

indicators.note: CO and I bank, i.e. store away, the letters between them

blocks.note: L is a pound, so two of them

annotation.surface: A swindler in business relies on a small sum of money.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On the fiddle' is slang for cheating, but here the fiddle is a violin. 'Banking' means holding in store.
annotation.definitionFit: Arcangelo Corelli was a Baroque composer and celebrated violinist.

clue.text: Left leader number 50 to get overthrown (5)

indicators.note: turned upside down, which in a down entry reverses the letters

blocks.note: any number will do; this one fits

annotation.surface: A left-wing leader is set to be deposed by the fifty.
annotation.walkthrough: Overthrowing fits a revolutionary, but it is the reversal instruction. Ninel was a real Soviet girls' name, Lenin backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Lenin led the Bolsheviks, the great leader of the political left.

clue.text: Son not showing up in brief class (3)

indicators.note: a son who is not showing up is absent, so S is missing from the word

blocks.note: a brief is a barrister, and a silk is a senior one (a KC)
the standard abbreviation, removed from SILK

annotation.surface: A son skips a short lesson.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brief' and 'class' suggest a short lesson; in fact a brief is British slang for a lawyer, and senior barristers are called silks after their gowns.
annotation.definitionFit: Ilk means kind or sort, as in 'people of that ilk'.

clue.text: Computer stores in area to the north reportedly near shop with alarm (5-3)

indicators.note: PC holds the other letters
in a down entry, going northward reverses the letters
what we hear, not what is written

blocks.note: IN plus A for area, running upward to give ANI
by means near, as in 'stand by me'

annotation.surface: A computer is kept in a northern district near a store with an alarm system.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shop with alarm' looks like a burglar alarm on a store; shop is the verb, and alarm is fear.
annotation.definitionFit: To panic-buy is to shop in a frightened rush, stockpiling in case supplies run out.

clue.text: Literary tale-teller working through holiday period (8)

indicators.note: ON runs through the middle of SUMMER

blocks.note: a machine that is on is working

annotation.surface: A novelist keeps writing through the summer break.
annotation.walkthrough: The tale-teller is one of Chaucer's pilgrims in The Canterbury Tales, not an author.
annotation.definitionFit: The Summoner is one of Chaucer's Canterbury pilgrims, and he tells a tale.

clue.text: Relatives loading recoiling weapon for zapping (6)

indicators.note: the relatives are loaded into the weapon
the weapon springs back, so its letters run backwards

blocks.note: reversed to NUG, then loaded with KIN

annotation.surface: Family members load a kicking gun to shoot something.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Recoiling' is exactly what a gun does, so it slips past as scenery; here it reverses GUN.
annotation.definitionFit: Nuking and zapping both mean destroying, or informally heating in a microwave.

clue.text: Flounder to shrivel up, moving tail forwards (6)

indicators.note: the final letter shifts towards the front

blocks.note: plants wither when they dry out

annotation.surface: A fish is told to shrink and swim tail first.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flounder' and 'tail' conjure a fish; flounder is the verb, to struggle helplessly.
annotation.definitionFit: To writhe and to flounder are both to twist and struggle about.

clue.text: Pitiful expression in ad removed from pine frontage (4,4)

indicators.note: something removed from a place is taken out of it, so AD comes out of FACADE

blocks.note: to pine for something is to long for it
removed from FACADE to leave FACE

annotation.surface: A sad look appears in an advert, taken off the front of a pine unit.
annotation.walkthrough: Pine is the verb meaning to yearn, not the wood that 'frontage' makes it seem.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: to pull a long face, mouth drawn down, is to look sad or disappointed.

clue.text: Choice cut of movie limited by filming on set differently (5,6)

indicators.note: the movie is hemmed in by the other letters
the letters of FILMING ON are set in a different order

annotation.surface: A film editor's favourite scene is shot on set in a new way.
annotation.walkthrough: The cut sounds like a film edit, but it is butchery. 'Set' is part of the anagram instruction, not fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Filet mignon is a prized small steak cut from the tenderloin.

clue.text: He, when cold, is quite ill, wanting temperature humid, possibly (6,6)

indicators.note: wanting in the sense of lacking: the fodder is without its T
the letters could be arranged another way

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation, removed from QUITE

annotation.surface: A man with a cold feels rather unwell and doesn't want his temperature taken in the damp.
annotation.walkthrough: 'He' looks like a sick man; it is the chemical symbol for helium, which is a liquid only when very cold.
annotation.definitionFit: Helium becomes liquid only at about four degrees above absolute zero.

clue.text: Protest from delinquent caned in haste heartlessly (3,3,3)

indicators.note: badly behaved, so the letters are out of order
the rearranged letters go inside
without a heart, so the central letter of the word is cut out

annotation.surface: A young offender who was beaten in a hurry has a complaint.
annotation.walkthrough: Delinquent is an adjective here, not a noun for the young offender, and haste gives HURRY, not the letters of 'haste'.
annotation.definitionFit: A hue and cry is a loud public outcry or protest.

clue.text: Like the original Mafia’s crime, receiving lashes (8)

definitions.note: The definition is an adjective ('like the original Mafia's'); the answer describes where they came from.

indicators.note: SIN takes the lashes inside it

annotation.surface: The old Mafia's wrongdoing was punished with a whipping.
annotation.walkthrough: Lashes suggests a flogging, but these are eyelashes, cilia.
annotation.definitionFit: The Mafia began in nineteenth-century Sicily, so by birthplace its first members were islanders from there.

clue.text: Trim new garment dresses individual raising issue (6,6)

indicators.note: the garment clothes the other letters

annotation.surface: A neat new outfit clothes someone who is raising a concern.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Raising issue' reads as bringing up a point; issue means children.
annotation.definitionFit: A single parent is one person bringing up their offspring alone.

clue.text: Princess’s part in opera with revolutionary finale (7)

definitions.note: Read 'Princess's' as 'Princess is', with the rest of the clue what she is.

indicators.note: turned round, so the letters reverse

blocks.note: a solo song in an opera

annotation.surface: A princess sings a role in an opera with a rousing, revolutionary ending.
annotation.walkthrough: Fittingly, Ariadne has her own opera, Strauss's Ariadne auf Naxos.
annotation.definitionFit: Ariadne was the Cretan princess who helped Theseus escape the labyrinth.

clue.text: Dope visiting Brussels and eastern US city (6)

indicators.note: GEN pays a visit inside the other letters

blocks.note: the European Union is based in Brussels
gen and dope both mean information

annotation.surface: A drug dealer travels between Brussels and an American city.
annotation.walkthrough: Dope sounds like drugs or a fool; here it is inside information, gen in British slang.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Oregon's second city, home of the state university, is one US city among many.

clue.text: Players worthy of the A team visit our ground (8)

definitions.text: Players worthy of the A team

indicators.note: ground down, so the letters are broken up

annotation.surface: Top-quality players come to visit our home stadium.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like a sports ground, but it is the past tense of grind.
annotation.definitionFit: Virtuosi are players of exceptional skill, good enough for the first team.

clue.text: Men amid boxing ring belted figure seen in the dark (5)

definitions.text: belted figure seen in the dark

indicators.note: boxing in the sense of putting into a box: IN encloses O

annotation.surface: Men around a boxing ring watch a prize-fighter with a belt at night.
annotation.walkthrough: The boxing ring and belt suggest a champion boxer; boxing is the container verb, and the belt is Orion's three stars.
annotation.definitionFit: Orion the Hunter is a constellation known for the three stars of his belt.

clue.text: Joke the wrong way about trouble or fix (4,2)

indicators.note: the joke's letters are reversed
the reversed joke goes round the trouble

annotation.surface: A joke taken badly might cause trouble or have to be fixed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Or' simply offers the definition as an alternative reading of the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: To nail something up is to fix it in place with nails.

clue.text: Korean side’s novel shot has no power (6)

indicators.note: the letter for power is absent

blocks.note: Kipling's novel about a boy in India
a chip is a short lofted golf shot
the physics symbol, removed from CHIP

annotation.surface: A Korean sports team's unusual shot lacks force.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Side' is a team in the surface but a side dish in the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Kimchi, fermented spiced cabbage, is the standard Korean side dish.

clue.text: Indication, forgetting line, one may need this? (3)

definitions.text: Indication, forgetting line, one may need this?

indicators.note: what you forget is left out, so L is dropped from CLUE

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation, removed from CLUE

annotation.surface: An actor who forgets a line may need a prompt.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: an actor forgetting a line needs a cue.
annotation.definitionFit: A cue is a signal or prompt, the thing a performer who dries needs.

clue.text: One may hold wine container, put off consuming it (8)

indicators.note: DETER swallows the container

blocks.note: a tin; 'it' refers back to this

annotation.surface: Someone is put off from drinking whatever is in a wine vessel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'It' stands for the container named earlier, so CAN goes inside DETER.
annotation.definitionFit: A decanter is a glass vessel holding wine for serving.

clue.text: Tolstoy heroine, with energy, squeezing figure’s sensitive appendages (8)

indicators.note: ANNA squeezes the number inside

annotation.surface: An energetic Tolstoy heroine hugs someone with a delicate shape.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Figure' suggests a body shape; it is a number.
annotation.definitionFit: Antennae are the sensitive feelers on an insect's head.

clue.text: Option for better tablets following wrench (6)

indicators.note: following means coming after, so EE is written after YANK

blocks.note: E is ecstasy, so two tablets

annotation.surface: Someone wants a better option than pills after twisting a joint.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Better' is not an improvement but one who bets. A Yankee is a bookmaker's bet combining four selections in eleven bets.
annotation.definitionFit: A Yankee is a multiple bet offered to punters at British bookmakers.
